steps.text: Look for a number that divides both 187 and 136. Both are multiples of 17.
11 and 8 share no factor other than 1, so the lowest form of 187/136 is 11/8.

hints: A portion is a fraction: (how many two-digit numbers are perfect squares) over (how many two-digit numbers there are).
The two-digit numbers run from 10 to 99: that is 99 − 9 = 90 numbers. Now list the two-digit squares, starting 4 × 4 = 16, and count them. Write the fraction and simplify it.
Similar: what portion of the one-digit numbers 1 to 9 are perfect squares? The squares are 1, 4 and 9, so it is 3 out of 9, which is 3/9 = 1/3.
All three fractions are equal. To get an equal fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number.
Compare 3/16 with ✻/96: what was 16 multiplied by to make 96? Multiply 3 by the same number. Then compare 3/16 with 12/△: what was 3 multiplied by to make 12?
Try a smaller one: the fractions ✻/12, 2/3 and 8/△ are all equal. 3 × 4 = 12, so ✻ = 2 × 4 = 8. And 2 × 4 = 8, so △ = 3 × 4 = 12.

steps.text: Equal fractions come from multiplying the top and bottom by the same number.

hints: The two fractions are equal. It is easier if you first write 45/36 in its lowest form.
Both 45 and 36 are in the 9 times table, so divide top and bottom by 9. Then ask: what must the new bottom number be multiplied by to make 32? Do the same to the top.
Try a smaller one: 6/9 and ✻/15 are equal. In lowest form 6/9 is 2/3. Since 3 × 5 = 15, ✻ = 2 × 5 = 10.

steps.text: Write 45/36 in lowest form: divide top and bottom by 9 to get 5/4.
Now 5/4 and ✻/32 are equal. 4 × 8 = 32, so multiply the top by 8 as well.
5 × 8 = 40, so the number in place of the asterisk is 40.

hints: Two equal fractions. First make 5/7 into an equal fraction with 42 at the bottom, so the tops can be compared.
7 × 6 = 42, so multiply the top of 5/7 by 6 as well. That number equals b − 8. To find b, add the 8 back.
Try a smaller one: (c − 2)/12 and 3/4 are equal. 4 × 3 = 12, so 3/4 = 9/12. Then c − 2 is 9, so c is 11.

steps.text: Make 5/7 into a fraction with 42 at the bottom: 7 × 6 = 42 and 5 × 6 = 30, so 5/7 = 30/42.
Now (b − 8)/42 and 30/42 are equal, so the tops are equal: b − 8 is 30.
Add 8 back: b = 30 + 8 = 38.

hints: The line runs from 0 to 2, not 0 to 1. So first find how long each of the 5 equal parts is.
Each part is 2 ÷ 5 = 2/5 long. Now count how many parts there are from 0 to point A on the number line, and add up that many parts.
Similar: a line from 0 to 3 is cut into 4 equal parts. Each part is 3/4. A point on the 3rd mark is at 3/4 + 3/4 + 3/4 = 9/4.

steps.text: The line from 0 to 2 is cut into 5 equal parts, so each part is 2 ÷ 5 = 2/5 long.
Point A is on the 2nd mark after 0, so it is 2 parts away from 0.
2/5 + 2/5 = 4/5, so point A represents 4/5.

hints: Before doing any working, compare each fraction with 1. Is the top smaller or bigger than the bottom?
When the top is smaller than the bottom, the fraction is less than 1. When the top is bigger than the bottom, the fraction is more than 1. Sort the four choices this way.
Similar: which is greatest of 5/6, 7/4 and 2/3? Only 7/4 has a top bigger than its bottom, so it is more than 1 and the others are less than 1. 7/4 is the greatest.

steps.text: Compare each fraction with 1.
In 19/21, 11/15 and 23/32 the top is smaller than the bottom, so each of them is less than 1.
In 9/8 the top is bigger than the bottom, so it is more than 1.
So the greatest fraction is 9/8.

hints: Compare each fraction with 1/2. A fraction is less than 1/2 when its top is less than half of its bottom.
Take 11/15: half of 15 is 7 1/2, and 11 is more than that, so 11/15 is more than 1/2. Do the same for the other three fractions.
Similar: which is smallest of 5/8, 4/9 and 7/12? Half of 8 is 4, half of 9 is 4 1/2, half of 12 is 6. Only 4/9 has a top below half its bottom, so 4/9 is the smallest.

steps.text: Compare each fraction with 1/2 by checking whether the top is more or less than half of the bottom.
11/15: half of 15 is 7 1/2, and 11 is more. 21/32: half of 32 is 16, and 21 is more. 17/28: half of 28 is 14, and 17 is more.
So those three are all more than 1/2.
14/29: half of 29 is 14 1/2, and 14 is less. So 14/29 is less than 1/2, and it is the smallest fraction.

hints: All four numerators are the same number. Think of sharing the same cake among more and more people: what happens to each share?
With the same top number, the more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each fraction is. So look at the four bottom numbers and decide which one cuts the whole into the most parts.
Similar: 5/3, 5/7 and 5/9 have the same top. Ninths are the smallest pieces, so 5/9 is the smallest of the three.
Put the five fractions in order from greatest to smallest. With five fractions, the middle one is the 3rd.
Use 1/2 and 1 as markers. 11/9 is more than 1. 14/28 is exactly 1/2. Now decide for 5/14, 13/21 and 3/7: is each one more than 1/2 or less than 1/2?
Similar: order 3/8, 5/4, 2/4, 5/6 and 1/3 from greatest. 5/4 is more than 1, 5/6 is more than 1/2, 2/4 is exactly 1/2, and 3/8 and 1/3 are less than 1/2. So the middle one is 2/4.

steps.text: Use 1/2 and 1 as markers. 11/9 is more than 1, so it is the greatest.
13/21 is more than 1/2, because half of 21 is 10 1/2 and 13 is more. It is less than 1, so it comes second.
14/28 is exactly 1/2, because 14 is half of 28.
3/7 and 5/14 are both less than 1/2 (half of 7 is 3 1/2, half of 14 is 7), so they come last.
In descending order the 3rd of the five fractions is 14/28, so 14/28 is in the middle.

hints: To compare fractions, give them all the same bottom number. Two of the choices are already in twenty-fourths, so change 1/3 and 5/8 into twenty-fourths as well.
For 1/3, multiply top and bottom by 8. For 5/8, multiply top and bottom by 3. Now you know the two tops your answer must lie between. Change 1/6 and 11/12 the same way.
Similar: which of 3/12, 7/12 and 11/12 is greater than 1/3 but less than 3/4? In twelfths, 1/3 is 4/12 and 3/4 is 9/12. Only 7/12 has a top between 4 and 9.

steps.text: Write everything in twenty-fourths. 1/3 = 8/24 and 5/8 = 15/24, so the top number must be more than 8 and less than 15.
1/6 = 4/24 (too small) and 11/12 = 22/24 (too big).
17/24 has a top of 17, which is more than 15, so it is too big.
13/24 has a top of 13, which lies between 8 and 15. So the fraction is 13/24.

hints: 'What should be added' is a missing-number question: take 3/8 away from 1 1/12 to find it.
First write 1 1/12 as an improper fraction: 12/12 + 1/12 = 13/12. Then give 13/12 and 3/8 the same bottom number (the smallest number that both 12 and 8 divide into) and subtract.
Try a smaller one: what should be added to 1/4 to get 1 1/6? 1 1/6 is 7/6. In twelfths, 7/6 = 14/12 and 1/4 = 3/12. 14/12 − 3/12 = 11/12.

steps.text: The number to add is 1 1/12 take away 3/8. Write 1 1/12 as 13/12.
The smallest number that both 12 and 8 divide into is 24. So 13/12 = 26/24 and 3/8 = 9/24.
So 17/24 should be added to 3/8.

hints: Split 7 3/8 into a whole-number part and a fraction part. The 6 on the left takes care of only some of the wholes.
7 3/8 − 6 = 1 3/8. So □/8 must equal 1 3/8. Change 1 3/8 into eighths: one whole is 8/8.
Try a smaller one: 2 + □/3 gives 4 1/3. Taking 2 away leaves 2 1/3. Two wholes are 6/3, and 6/3 + 1/3 = 7/3, so □ = 7.

steps.text: Take 6 away from 7 3/8: that leaves 1 3/8. So □/8 must equal 1 3/8.
So the number in the box is 11.

hints: Split 11 1/5 into wholes and a fraction. The 8 on the left covers only some of the wholes; the rest must come from □/5.
11 1/5 − 8 = 3 1/5. So □/5 must equal 3 1/5. Change 3 1/5 into fifths: each whole is 5/5.
Try a smaller one: 5 + □/4 gives 7 3/4. Taking 5 away leaves 2 3/4. Two wholes are 8/4, and 8/4 + 3/4 = 11/4, so □ = 11.

steps.text: Take 8 away from 11 1/5: that leaves 3 1/5. So □/5 must equal 3 1/5.
Three wholes are 15/5, so 3 1/5 = 15/5 + 1/5 = 16/5.
So the number in the box is 16.

hints: The two fractions have the same bottom number, so you add only the tops. And a fraction equals 1 when its top and bottom are the same.
Add the tops: 7 + 2. The sum of the two fractions is that total over ✻. What must ✻ be for the fraction to equal 1?
Similar: 3/✻ and 2/✻ add up to 1. The tops add to 5, so the sum is 5/✻. That equals 1 when ✻ = 5, because 5/5 = 1.

steps.text: The fractions have the same bottom number, so add the tops: 7 + 2 = 9. The sum is 9/✻.
A fraction equals 1 when the top and the bottom are the same number.

hints: First add the three fractions on the left: same bottom number, so add the tops. Then turn the result into an equal fraction with 33 at the bottom.
1/11 + 1/11 + 1/11 = 3/11. Now 11 × 3 = 33, so multiply the top by 3 as well.
Similar: 1/5 + 1/5 is the same as ✻/20. The left side is 2/5. Since 5 × 4 = 20, ✻ = 2 × 4 = 8.

steps.text: Add the tops on the left: 1/11 + 1/11 + 1/11 = 3/11.
Change 3/11 into thirty-thirds: 11 × 3 = 33, so multiply the top by 3 too.
3 × 3 = 9, so 3/11 = 9/33 and the asterisk is 9.

hints: Add the three fractions on the left first. They share a bottom number, so only the tops are added. Then make an equal fraction with 12 at the bottom.
5/4 + 5/4 + 5/4 = 15/4. Now 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 as well.
Similar: 3/2 + 3/2 is the same as ✻/10. The left side is 6/2. Since 2 × 5 = 10, ✻ = 6 × 5 = 30.

steps.text: Add the tops on the left: 5/4 + 5/4 + 5/4 = 15/4.
Change 15/4 into twelfths: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 too.
15 × 3 = 45, so 15/4 = 45/12 and the asterisk is 45.

hints: The four fractions on the left have the same bottom number, 7. Make the right side into sevenths too, so the tops can be compared.
Divide the top and bottom of 48/28 by 4 to get a fraction in sevenths. The four equal tops on the left must add up to its top.
Similar: three lots of ✻/5 add up to 18/15. Dividing top and bottom by 3, 18/15 = 6/5. Three equal tops add up to 6, so ✻ is 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

steps.text: Write 48/28 in sevenths: divide top and bottom by 4 to get 12/7.
On the left, the four fractions have the same bottom number, so their tops add up: four equal tops make 12.

hints: Like fractions have the same denominator, so you add only the numerators and keep the denominator.
Add the numerators: 3 + 5 + 6 = 14. So the sum is 14 over the denominator. What denominator makes that fraction equal to 2?
Similar: like fractions with numerators 1, 2 and 5 add up to 4. The tops add to 8, so the sum is 8 over the denominator. 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the denominator is 2 (8/2 = 4).

steps.text: Like fractions share one denominator, so add the numerators: 3 + 5 + 6 = 14.
The sum is 14 over the denominator, and it equals 2. So 14 divided by the denominator is 2.
14 ÷ 2 = 7, so the denominator is 7. Check: 14/7 = 2.

hints: Two jobs first: pick the smallest fraction in group A and the greatest in group B. Then multiply them.

In group A every top is 7, so the biggest bottom number gives the smallest fraction. In group B every bottom is 8, so the biggest top gives the greatest fraction. Multiply your two picks: top × top and bottom × bottom, then simplify.
Similar: multiply 2/9 by 6/8. First 6/8 = 3/4. Then 2/9 × 3/4 = 6/36 = 1/6.

steps.text: Group A: every top is 7, so the biggest bottom gives the smallest fraction: 7/12.
Group B: every bottom is 8, so the biggest top gives the greatest fraction: 6/8, which is 3/4 in lowest form.
Divide top and bottom by 3: 21/48 = 7/16. So the product is 7/16.

hints: The three fractions have different bottom numbers. Change them all to the same bottom number before you subtract and add.
12 is in the 3 times table and the 4 times table, so use twelfths: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12. Now work out 11/12 − 8/12 + 3/12 from left to right, and simplify.
Try a smaller one: 5/6 − 1/2 + 1/3. In sixths that is 5/6 − 3/6 + 2/6 = 4/6, which is 2/3 in lowest form.

steps.text: Put the values in: x − y + z is 11/12 − 2/3 + 1/4.
Change to twelfths: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.
6/12 in lowest form is 1/2, so the value is 1/2.

hints: Work out the right side first. Then m is that answer with 1/4 added back, because 1/4 was taken away from m.
Right side: change 3/5 into twentieths (multiply top and bottom by 4), then subtract it from 13/20. To that result, add 1/4, also written in twentieths, and simplify.
Try a smaller one: n − 1/3 equals 5/6 − 1/2. Right side: 5/6 − 3/6 = 2/6. Add 1/3 back: 2/6 + 2/6 = 4/6, so n is 2/3.

steps.text: So m with 1/4 taken away is 1/20. To find m, add 1/4 back.
6/20 in lowest form is 3/10, so m = 3/10.

hints: Follow BODMAS: do 'of' first, then ÷ and ×, and only then + and −. Here 'of' means multiply.
Work out three pieces separately: 2/9 of 27/20, then 2/7 ÷ 5/14 (to divide by a fraction, flip it and multiply), then 3/4 × 1/5. Last, put the three results over 20 and add and subtract.

steps.text: Multiplication: 3/4 × 1/5 = 3/20.
So the expression simplifies to 13/20.

hints: The hour hand takes one whole hour, 60 minutes, to move from 9 to 10. So how far it has gone tells you how much of the hour has passed.
The hand has gone two-fifths of the way, so two-fifths of 60 minutes have passed since 9 o'clock. Find one-fifth of 60 first, then double it.
Similar: if the hour hand were three-quarters of the way from 4 to 5, then 3/4 of 60 minutes have passed. One quarter is 15 minutes, so that is 45 minutes: the time is 4:45.

steps.text: The hour hand moves from 9 to 10 in one hour, which is 60 minutes.
It is two-fifths of the way, so two-fifths of 60 minutes have passed since 9 o'clock.
One-fifth of 60 minutes is 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes, so two-fifths is 2 × 12 = 24 minutes.
So the correct time is 24 minutes past 9, which is 9:24.

hints: 'Four-ninths of a number is 24' means 4 of the 9 equal parts of the number add up to 24. Find one part first.
4 parts make 24, so 1 part is 24 ÷ 4 = 6. The whole number is 9 parts. Find it, then take half.
Try a smaller one: two-fifths of a number is 8. One fifth is 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so the number is 5 × 4 = 20, and half of it is 10.

steps.text: Four-ninths of the number is 24, so 4 of its 9 equal parts make 24.
One part is 24 ÷ 4 = 6.
The whole number is 9 parts: 9 × 6 = 54.
Half of 54 is 54 ÷ 2 = 27. So half of the number is 27.

hints: 3/5 of the exercise takes 24 minutes. Find how long 1/5 takes, then how long the whole exercise (5/5) takes.
3 fifths take 24 minutes, so 1 fifth takes 24 ÷ 3 = 8 minutes. Multiply by 5 for the whole exercise, then count that many minutes on from 11 am.
Try a smaller one: 2/3 of a job takes 10 minutes. 1/3 takes 10 ÷ 2 = 5 minutes, so the whole job takes 3 × 5 = 15 minutes. Starting at 2 pm, it ends at 2:15 pm.

steps.text: 3/5 of the exercise takes 24 minutes, so 1/5 takes 24 ÷ 3 = 8 minutes.
The whole exercise is 5/5, so it takes 5 × 8 = 40 minutes.
40 minutes after 11 am is 11:40 am. So she will complete the exercise at 11:40 am.

hints: The 120 litres fill the EMPTY part of the tank. So first find what fraction of the tank is empty.
If 4/7 is full, then 7/7 − 4/7 = 3/7 is empty. So 3 of the 7 equal parts hold 120 litres. Find one part, then all 7 parts.
Try a smaller one: a jug is 3/5 full and needs 4 litres more to fill it. The empty part is 2/5, so 1/5 is 4 ÷ 2 = 2 litres and the full jug holds 5 × 2 = 10 litres.

steps.text: The tank is 4/7 full, so the empty part is 7/7 − 4/7 = 3/7 of the tank.
That empty 3/7 holds 120 litres, so 1/7 of the tank is 120 ÷ 3 = 40 litres.
The whole tank is 7 parts: 7 × 40 = 280.
So the total capacity of the tank is 280 litres.

hints: Rs. 2700 is 3 of the 5 equal parts of his money. So what is left in the account is the other 2 parts.
3 parts make Rs. 2700, so 1 part is Rs. 2700 ÷ 3 = Rs. 900. How many parts are still in the account? Multiply.
Try a smaller one: Rs. 60 is three-quarters of Meena's money. One quarter is 60 ÷ 3 = 20, so Rs. 20. She has 1 quarter left, so her balance is Rs. 20.

steps.text: Rs. 2700 is three-fifths of the total, so 3 of the 5 equal parts make Rs. 2700.
One part is 2700 ÷ 3 = 900, so one-fifth is Rs. 900.
After the withdrawal, 5 − 3 = 2 parts are left in the account.
2 × 900 = 1800, so the balance is Rs. 1800.

hints: First find what fraction of the class went to the playground. Those are the 14 students.
Library and lab together are 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7 of the class, so the playground group is the remaining 2/7. If 2 parts are 14 students, how many is 1 part? The library group is 3 parts.
Try a smaller one: 1/5 of a class sing, 2/5 dance and the remaining 12 paint. The painters are 2/5, so 1/5 is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 students. The dancers are 2 × 6 = 12.

steps.text: Library and science lab together: 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7 of the class.
So the playground group is 7/7 − 5/7 = 2/7 of the class, and that is 14 students.
One-seventh of the class is 14 ÷ 2 = 7 students.
The library group is 3/7 of the class: 3 × 7 = 21. So 21 students went to the library.

hints: Add up the fractions for roses, sunflowers and marigolds. What is left over is the fraction for the 30 hibiscus plants.
2/9 + 1/9 + 4/9 = 7/9, so the hibiscus plants are the remaining 2/9. If 2 parts are 30 plants, find 1 part. Sunflowers and marigolds together are 1 + 4 = 5 parts.
Try a smaller one: 1/6 of the fruit are apples, 2/6 are pears and the remaining 12 are plums. Plums are 3/6, so 1/6 is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Apples and pears together are 3 parts: 3 × 4 = 12.

steps.text: Roses, sunflowers and marigolds together: 2/9 + 1/9 + 4/9 = 7/9 of the plants.
So the hibiscus plants are 9/9 − 7/9 = 2/9 of the plants, and that is 30 plants.
One-ninth of the plants is 30 ÷ 2 = 15.
Sunflowers and marigolds together are 1/9 + 4/9 = 5/9, which is 5 × 15 = 75.
So there are 75 sunflower and marigold plants in all.

hints: First find the size of one small part of the tank. 5/8 full means 5 of the tank's 8 equal parts hold 120 litres.
5 parts hold 120 litres, so 1 part holds 120 ÷ 5 = 24 litres. Find the full tank (8 parts), then take 2/3 of it.
Try a smaller one: a tank that is 3/4 full holds 30 litres. 1/4 is 30 ÷ 3 = 10 litres, so the full tank holds 40 litres. When it is 1/2 full it holds 20 litres.

steps.text: 5/8 of the tank is 120 litres, so 1/8 of the tank is 120 ÷ 5 = 24 litres.
The full tank is 8 parts: 8 × 24 = 192 litres.
One-third of 192 is 192 ÷ 3 = 64 litres, so two-thirds is 2 × 64 = 128 litres.
So the tank holds 128 litres when it is 2/3 full.

hints: Start with the children: if 3/5 of the visitors were adults, what fraction were children? That fraction is the 120 children.
Children are 5/5 − 3/5 = 2/5 of the visitors. 2 parts are 120, so 1 part is 120 ÷ 2 = 60 visitors. Adults are 3 parts. Then find 5/9 of the adults.
Try a smaller one: 2/3 of the visitors are adults and there are 10 children. Children are 1/3, so adults are 2 × 10 = 20. If 3/4 of the adults are women, that is 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15 women.

steps.text: 3/5 of the visitors were adults, so 5/5 − 3/5 = 2/5 were children. That is 120 children.
One-fifth of the visitors is 120 ÷ 2 = 60, so the adults (3/5) number 3 × 60 = 180.
5/9 of the adults were female. One-ninth of 180 is 180 ÷ 9 = 20.
5 × 20 = 100, so 100 female adults visited the zoo.

hints: Take it in order: find the total stock, take off what Mr. Joshi bought, and then take a quarter off what REMAINS (not off the total).
Total stock: 308 + 52 = 360 kg. Mr. Joshi buys 2/5 of 360: one-fifth is 360 ÷ 5 = 72 kg, so double it. Subtract to find what remains, then take away a quarter of that.
Try a smaller one: a shop has 40 kg. It sells 1/4 (10 kg), leaving 30 kg. Then it sells 1/3 of the remainder (10 kg). 30 − 10 = 20 kg are left.

steps.text: Total stock: 308 + 52 = 360 kg.
Mr. Joshi buys 2/5 of 360 kg. One-fifth is 360 ÷ 5 = 72 kg, so he buys 2 × 72 = 144 kg.
Remaining: 360 − 144 = 216 kg.
Mr. Shinde buys a quarter of the remaining 216 kg: 216 ÷ 4 = 54 kg.
Left with the grocer: 216 − 54 = 162 kg.

hints: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999. Count all of them first, then think about how many are even.
Count them all: 999 − 100 + 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are even. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are even.

steps.text: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
Count them all, counting both ends: 999 − 100 + 1 = 900.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are even: 900 ÷ 2 = 450.
So there are 450 3-digit even numbers.
Pages 1 to 9: 9 pages with 1 digit each, so 9 × 1 = 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 99: 90 pages with 2 digits each, so 90 × 2 = 180 digits.
Page 100 is the only page with 3 digits, so it uses 3 digits.
Add them up: 9 + 180 + 3 = 192. So 192 digits are used.

hints: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999. You need to count every number from one to the other.
To count from 100 to 999, subtract and then add 1, so that both ends are counted: 999 − 100 + 1.
Try a smaller one: from 5 to 9 there are 9 − 5 + 1 = 5 numbers. Count them to check: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

steps.text: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
Count from 100 to 999, counting both ends: 999 − 100 + 1 = 900.
So there are 900 3-digit numbers in all.

hints: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99. Count all of them first, then think about how many are even.
Count them all: 99 − 10 + 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are even. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are even.

steps.text: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99.
Count them all, counting both ends: 99 − 10 + 1 = 90.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are even: 90 ÷ 2 = 45.
So there are 45 2-digit even numbers.

hints: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999. You need to count every number from one to the other.
To count from 1000 to 9999, subtract and then add 1, so that both ends are counted: 9999 − 1000 + 1.
Try a smaller one: from 5 to 9 there are 9 − 5 + 1 = 5 numbers. Count them to check: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

steps.text: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999.
Count from 1000 to 9999, counting both ends: 9999 − 1000 + 1 = 9000.
So there are 9000 4-digit numbers in all.

hints: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999. Count all of them first, then think about how many are odd.
Count them all: 9999 − 1000 + 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are odd. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are odd.

steps.text: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999.
Count them all, counting both ends: 9999 − 1000 + 1 = 9000.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are odd: 9000 ÷ 2 = 4500.
So there are 4500 4-digit odd numbers.

hints: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99. You need to count every number from one to the other.
To count from 10 to 99, subtract and then add 1, so that both ends are counted: 99 − 10 + 1.
Try a smaller one: from 5 to 9 there are 9 − 5 + 1 = 5 numbers. Count them to check: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

steps.text: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99.
Count from 10 to 99, counting both ends: 99 − 10 + 1 = 90.
So there are 90 2-digit numbers in all.

hints: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999. Count all of them first, then think about how many are odd.
Count them all: 999 − 100 + 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are odd. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are odd.

steps.text: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
Count them all, counting both ends: 999 − 100 + 1 = 900.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are odd: 900 ÷ 2 = 450.
So there are 450 3-digit odd numbers.

hints: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999. Count all of them first, then think about how many are even.
Count them all: 9999 − 1000 + 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are even. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are even.

steps.text: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999.
Count them all, counting both ends: 9999 − 1000 + 1 = 9000.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are even: 9000 ÷ 2 = 4500.
So there are 4500 4-digit even numbers.

hints: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99. Count all of them first, then think about how many are odd.

hints: Supplementary angles are two angles that sit together on a straight line. What do the angles on a straight line add up to?
The two angles add up to 180°. One of them is 156°. So ask: 156° plus what makes 180°? You can find it by taking 156 away from 180.
Try another one: the supplementary angle of 110° is 70°, because 180° − 110° = 70°. Check: 110° + 70° = 180°.

HCF means Highest Common Factor: the biggest number that divides both 12 and 18 exactly, with nothing left over.
Write down every number that divides 12 exactly. These are its factors, and they come in pairs: 1 × 12 is one pair. Do the same for 18. Then look for the biggest number that is on both lists.
